title: CtRL-Sim: Reactive and Controllable Driving Agents with Offline Reinforcement Learning

control_signal.value: Exponential tilting coefficients kappa, one per factored reward component (goal reached, vehicle-vehicle collision, vehicle-road-edge collision), positive or negative.

control_mechanism.value: The model predicts a return-to-go distribution per agent; at sampling time that distribution is exponentially tilted by kappa, then actions are sampled conditioned on it. Optional fine-tuning on CAT collision scenes strengthens adversarial control.

base_model.value: Return-conditioned multi-agent autoregressive encoder-decoder Transformer over tokenised actions and returns, with future-state prediction head; run in Nocturne extended with a Box2D physics engine.

datasets.value: Offline RL dataset built from Waymo Open Motion Dataset via Nocturne; 1000 random test scenes; fine-tuning on CAT-generated long-tail collision scenes.

metrics.value: ADE, FDE, goal success rate, JSD, collision and offroad rate, generation time; controllability by goal success, collision and offroad rates matching the tilted reward axis.

controllability_evidence.value: Tilting kappa from -25 to 25 gives a relatively monotonic change in each metric; at -25 the fine-tuned model produces 2.1x as many collisions and 1.8x as many offroad violations as the base model.

stated_limitations.value: Inference latency may make large-scale RL training expensive; controls behaviour but not initial agent placement; extreme tilting (-50) gives erratic, implausible behaviour; imitation drift can push agents off road.
